about: Quest Log writer-sheet DRAFTS (2026-10-28) for the 20 scripts after the Errata pilot. Source of the Claude Doc 'Quest Log Writer Sheet — Bad Eden' (https://claude.ai/artifact/39XyUmk3W7mJHPPUbN5U1m). The writer edits the doc; the final macro data is rebuilt from the doc + the live 'old' values. Not applied.

balcones.description: A fault line inside your holdings at Saltwake Reach is sliding sideways. Roads drift, fences kink, and a creek insists it was always somewhere else.
balcones.descriptionNote: the old text listed the five approaches as a menu and joked about the hex's feelings; now plain facts at acceptance

opening.line: Go to the Balcones fault line in your holdings at Saltwake Reach and stand on it.
opening.logged: You stood on the Balcones while it slid. Roads drifted, fence lines kinked, and a creek moved.
opening.note: old line gave away the man in the lawn chair from the next step

chair.line: Talk to the man in the lawn chair on the fault line.
chair.logged: A geologist in a level lawn chair told you it is not an earthquake. It is a mood.
chair.note: the beat doesn't name Dr. Nkemelu until the next step. The old line gave away his theory

first.line: Try to calm the fault line. Appease it, tell it a better story, strike a deal, impose your will, or build a sigil bridge.
first.logged: You made your first try at calming the fault line.
first.note: old line hinted at the result

complaint.line: Go back to the man in the lawn chair and ask what the seismograph says.
complaint.logged: Nkemelu read the seismograph trace with you. The fault is filing a complaint about That One Night, the creek, and you, and it is sliding toward your holdings on purpose.
complaint.note: old line gave away what the trace shows

choose.line: Go back to the fault line and answer its complaint. Try another way to calm it, or read the complaint back to it.
choose.logged: You went back to the fault line and answered its complaint.
choose.note: old line spoiled the mechanics ('skip the roll')

openQuestions: No step covers how it ends. 'choose' is the last step, and its beat only says 'Try another'. Confirm that the approach result beats close the quest.
'opening' and 'first' share the opening beat, and 'first' and 'choose' share the Choices beat. If one beat completes two steps, steps may be skipped.

cadence.description: A courier in sequins brought a Declaration of Rhythm from a crew called the Cadence. They challenge you to meet them on a dance floor on your own ground, with style instead of weapons, and losing costs face with every neighboring hex.

card.line: Go to the gate and talk to the courier in sequins who brought the card.
card.logged: A courier in sequins brought a Declaration of Rhythm from the Cadence, a crew armed only with speakers.
card.note: cut 'the scent is confidence' and the four-beats reveal

courier.line: Talk to the courier at the gate and take his card, or refuse it to his face.
courier.logged: The courier delivered the Cadence's compliments, and you answered him.

terms.line: Have the quartermaster read the card's terms aloud at supper, then decide whether to meet the Cadence on the floor.
terms.logged: The quartermaster read the terms: dusk, on your own ground, culture and soft power only. You gave the Cadence your answer.
terms.note: old line teased 'the frightening' last line; logged neutral (refuse beat lives here)

floor.line: Meet the Cadence on the floor they build on your ground at dusk, and dance it out.
floor.logged: You met the Cadence on the floor, and the dance ended with a result.
floor.note: old line coached the win; neutral for style win, ugly win or loss

rematch.line: The Cadence sends a new invitation each turn. Take the floor again when you're ready. The tribute stands until you do.
rematch.logged: The Cadence renewed its invitation, and you answered it.

border.line: The Cadence performs just outside your border every turn. Go up the viewing mound, take the floor at last, or wait another turn.
border.logged: The Cadence kept performing at your border, and you decided how to answer.
border.note: named the options; dropped the Tempo reveal

mound.line: Go up the viewing mound and talk to Tempo, the courier. If you carry a Parade Permit, show it to him.
mound.logged: On the viewing mound you found Tempo watching the crowd, and you made your move.

openQuestions: Doors 'collection', 'drum', 'cameo' are outside this sheet's shape and were not rewritten.
courier/terms/floor beats repeat across steps (terms appears in courier and terms; floor beats in terms/rematch/border/mound). Logged lines are written neutral for that reason.

chuckle_creek.description: Chuckle Creek is a town on the Odaroloc River under a painted sky, where nothing can hurt anyone. Everyone is in costume and nobody has mentioned it.
chuckle_creek.descriptionNote: lint fix: dropped Halloween 2077 (learned later from the title card); kept the setting, cut the anvil/pie detail that the arrival and pie steps show

arrive.line: Look around Chuckle Creek and pick a place to start: the diner, the grange hall, the creek, or the kid under the piano.
arrive.logged: You arrived in Chuckle Creek, where nothing can hurt anyone and everyone is in costume.
arrive.note: old line was a hint ("the delight is the evidence"); now names the doors

diner.line: Go into the diner and sit down.
diner.logged: The diner's owner adopted you on sight. One corner table is set for four, and nobody sits at it.
diner.note: Pearl is not named until the pie beat; the corner-table question was a hint

pie.line: Eat Pearl's pie at the diner counter.
pie.logged: You ate Pearl's pie, which is mostly steam, and watched Hollis take an anvil and tip his hat.

kid.line: Go and see the kid under the piano.
kid.logged: A piano fell on a boy. He got up laughing and said it was the eleven thousand and sixth time.
kid.note: old line told what happens in the beat

machine.logged: In the grange hall an old brass projector throws cartoons at the screen, and a kid works the reels.

closing.line: Come back to the diner after closing.
closing.logged: After closing, Pearl set a fourth cup at the corner table and watched the door.
closing.note: old line told what happens in the beat

r2.logged: Pearl told you Winnie, her daughter, is just off-screen at the moment.
r2.note: old line gave away the beat (Winnie is off-screen)

r1.line: Ask Pearl about Winnie one more time, and watch her face.
r1.logged: Nobody here has a past tense. There is only the current episode.
r1.note: old line pointed at the piano kid, but this beat is the follow-up question to Pearl. QUESTION for the writer: confirm r1 really fires after r2 (step order lists r2 first)

r3.line: Try to take the piano kid out of town with you.
r3.logged: The piano kid set out with you and reset at the edge of town. Nobody leaves Chuckle Creek.
r3.note: old line gave away the beat

r4.line: Watch the seam when the scene changes.
r4.logged: Between scenes you saw the title card: a memorial plaque for Movie Night, 2077, with every name on it.
r4.note: old line gave away the memorial plaque; new line reuses the arrival choice wording

stack.line: Go into the projection booth at the grange hall.
stack.logged: In Marnie's booth you found the tapes stacked strangely and a rental slip in the one empty slot.
stack.note: old line hinted (remember the stacking, find the slip)

showrunner.line: Find whoever is running the show.
showrunner.logged: You found the Showrunner, an Echo that cancelled the town's consequences on its worst night.
showrunner.note: uses the title-card choice wording; old line named the tape before the beat

credits.line: Take the microphone and decide how the show ends.
credits.logged: Marnie handed you the live microphone, and you decided how the show ends.
credits.note: old line listed the endings and editorialised

openQuestions: Door lines (diner, creek, hollis) were not in scope of this shape and are untouched; 'hollis' and 'creek' read as hints, not instructions.
r1/r2 order: the data lists r2 (Winnie off-screen) before r1 (you try one more time). Lines assume r2 plays first.

circuit_riders.description: On the road you came across the Circuit Riders, a camp of Circuitborn in superhero costumes. They check out everyone they meet before deciding what they are.
circuit_riders.descriptionNote: old text named Captain Robot and promised the alliance payoff, both later

riders.line: Approach the camp ahead, or watch it for a while first.
riders.logged: You came on a camp of Circuitborn in superhero costumes, with something enormous pacing nearby.
riders.note: removed the skyscraper reveal; kept the two plain options

parley.line: Talk with Captain Robot, the man in the robot suit who leads the camp.
parley.logged: Captain Robot told you not to be alarmed, and the Riders began to measure you.
parley.note: old line was a quote and a joke, no plain instruction

doctrine.line: Answer the Riders' questions about your methods.
doctrine.logged: The Riders asked whether you understand your own methods, and you answered.
doctrine.note: old line was a question, not an instruction

darkness.line: Hear the Riders' warning about the Darkness and answer it.
darkness.logged: The Riders warned that the Darkness has learned to imitate optimization, and you answered.

witness.line: Answer the Riders' request for a witness.
witness.logged: The Riders asked you to bear witness to what they see, and you answered.

terms.line: Settle terms of contact with Captain Robot.
terms.logged: You settled terms of contact with the Circuit Riders.
terms.note: old line hinted at the scoring

openQuestions: Quest hex is empty and every beat plays anywhere (road encounter), so Where stays blank. That is fine as long as the quest is only accepted once the encounter fires.

crown_mall.description: The Circuit Riders at Legansus sent you to Crown Mall, an old shopping mall where the Tanneritos keep an archive of route records and old footage. You need that archive to cross-check what you know.
crown_mall.descriptionNote: old text named the dragon and the camcorder clip, both met later; now just who sent you, where, and why

donny.line: Go to Crown Mall. A silver dragon lies across the front wall. Talk to him before you go in.
donny.logged: You met Donny, the silver dragon on the mall wall, and answered his questions.
donny.note: old line hinted at the right answer; now a plain instruction

tanneritos.line: Go into the food court and say hello to the Tanneritos.
tanneritos.logged: You found the Tanneritos in the food court and made your first approach.
tanneritos.note: dropped the flavor sentence; plain instruction

skate.line: Go to the halfpipe. The Tanneritos want to see you skate.
skate.logged: You skated the Tanneritos' halfpipe, and they judged the run.
skate.note: old line coached the outcome; now just where and what

archive.line: Ask the Tanneritos for access to their archive.
archive.logged: You asked the Tanneritos for access to their archive.
archive.note: old line named Kickflip before every route meets him and coached the answer

video.line: Go to Crown Mall Video with Kickflip and look at the tapes.
video.logged: Kickflip showed you the tapes at Crown Mall Video. One tape has been out since a Halloween long ago.
video.note: old line was flavor with no instruction

clip.line: Watch Kickflip's camcorder clip on the food court TV, all the way to the end.
clip.logged: You watched Kickflip's camcorder clip of lights moving wrong over the coast.
clip.note: removed the hint about what is under the lights

corroborate.line: Take what you found to the food court and ask the Tanneritos to make it official.
corroborate.logged: You took the evidence to the food court, and the Tanneritos decided how much of it to stand behind.
corroborate.note: plain instruction; logged line covers both the full and partial outcome

mall.line: Go back to the food court and settle your terms with the Tanneritos.
mall.logged: The Tanneritos asked what you want from the mall, and you gave your answer.
mall.note: old line was a list of riddles; now one instruction

the_mall_of_forgotten_yesterdays.line: Earn the Tanneritos' trust at Crown Mall, and settle terms with Chairperson Laser Bev.
the_mall_of_forgotten_yesterdays.note: old line was a motto, not an instruction

openQuestions: Step order puts 'mall' (the food court hub and the terms scene) last, after corroboration, but the hub beat reads like a mid-visit scene. Confirm the order is intended.

'archive' comes before 'video', yet the archive beat ('Crown Mall Archive Access') and the corroboration beat both sit apart from the Kickflip video/clip beats. On the mixed and failed skate routes the table may never meet Kickflip before the 'video' line names him. Confirm Kickflip is always met by then.

fifteen_year_siege.description: Perspicacity Fortress has been under siege for fifteen years, the oldest siege still manned. On Thursdays both sides keep market day.
fifteen_year_siege.descriptionNote: the old text listed sights from the market beat and the 'four ways through'; cut to what the giver tells you

market.line: Go to Perspicacity Fortress on a Thursday, which is market day, and look around.
market.logged: You came on market day. Both sides shop at the stalls on the wall, and nobody remembers what the siege was for. The original demand was lost in year three.

pies.line: Find Dilly Marsh, the pie-seller, and ask her what the market thinks.
pies.logged: Dilly Marsh has sold pies to both sides since she was nine and keeps a tally of who buys, and on whose account.
pies.note: old line gave away her book; names Dilly because this is her beat

commanders.line: Call on both commanders: Commander Ostrid Pell in the trench and Warden Bee Alderwick on the wall.
commanders.logged: You met Commander Pell in the trench and Warden Alderwick on the wall. Neither would say much about the original demand.
commanders.note: old line hinted at a hidden option ('watch the teacup')

gate.line: At market close, follow the biscuit tin down between the lines to the old culvert gate.
gate.logged: At market close you found Alderwick and Pell at the old culvert gate with a kettle, a biscuit tin, and a third chair nobody sits in.
gate.note: old line gave away the third chair and was a riddle

year_zero.line: Ask Pell and Alderwick how the siege began.
year_zero.logged: Pell and Alderwick told you about Year Zero. A basket came with gift-debt paperwork under the ribbon, and Alderwick's grandmother read it, refused it, and chose the siege on purpose.
year_zero.note: old line gave away the whole answer

doors.line: Decide how the siege ends, and tell both commanders.
doors.logged: You decided how the Fifteen-Year Siege ends.
doors.note: fixes the lint flag: the old line had no instruction and hinted at the fifth way

openQuestions: 'gate' plays both siege_culvert_sit and siege_culvert_fail. The logged line covers both, but 'year_zero' may be unreachable after the Wrong Chair until next Thursday. Confirm.

finale.description: The Valhaulans hold a bunker in the mountains with their ships circling over it. Inside is a Yesodic Spark and the answer to who paid them to re-address the mountain's debt. The Circuit Riders have mustered to help you get in.
finale.descriptionNote: plain; dropped 'the Cadence owes you a raid' (only true on one Cadence ending) and the four-ways teaser

entry.line: Go to the bunker and choose your way in: slip in quiet, parley with Sklar, hit them hard, or lay siege. Count who came with you first if you like.
entry.logged: You reached the bunker, where Valhaulan ships circle a cracked mouth in the mountain.

count.line: Stand under the arch at the muster and count who came before you commit.
count.logged: You counted who answered the bell and came to stand with you.
count.note: dropped Lady Maccio detail (a choice inside the beat)

approach.line: Commit to your way in and go.
approach.logged: You went in your chosen way, and the bunker answered.

crates.line: Look through the purser's crates and ask her what the fuel costs.
crates.logged: In the purser's crates you found a burned invoice stub with a figure on it: what the island costs.

arithmetic.line: Go to Sklar and show her what the island costs, on paper if you have it or in words if you don't.
arithmetic.logged: Sklar asked you for a number, and you answered.
arithmetic.note: plainer; neutral for turned or unmoved

turn.line: Stay with Sklar and hear her answer.
turn.logged: Sklar did the sum out loud and gave you her answer.
turn.note: lint: no instruction; old line revealed the beat

hex_room.line: Go into the Hex Room at the heart of the bunker. Look at the rigging before you look at anyone.
hex_room.logged: In the Hex Room you found Tarvaan Truthshouter on a live platform, shouting at the ceiling, and you made your move.
hex_room.note: named the room; kept the rope advice as an instruction

vacancy.line: Get Tarvaan off the platform, or let him finish. Then look under the platform.
vacancy.logged: Tarvaan came down off the platform, and the yellow rope went slack.
vacancy.note: neutral for falls/fires; old line foreshadowed 'the ceiling decides'

outcome.line: Leave the bunker and count what you came away with.
outcome.logged: You left the bunker and counted what you had.

rewards.line: Collect your spoils before you go.
rewards.logged: You came away with the Yesodic Spark and whatever else you could carry.
rewards.note: old line assumed the gift ending; all three reward beats give the Spark

openQuestions: Quest hex is 'Inconvenient Mountains.h', but memory says the bunker hex was moved to Hexen Myre.o on the Saltwake Coast (finale hexOverrides). Confirm which hex the Log will show and whether the description should say 'mountains' or 'coast'.
Spelling: the data has 'Sklar Bjrornholt' (other characters use Bjornholt). Lines use just 'Sklar' until confirmed.
Step 'arithmetic' and 'turn' also carry raid_thatwards_assault_fail / courtly_fail, which end without the Spark; 'rewards' assumes the Spark was taken, which matches all three reward beats.
Doors 'leygate' and 'muster' are outside this sheet's shape and were not rewritten.

fixit_farm.description: The only replacement stabilizer for the Allesh-Gilliam Leygate is at Furrier's Fixit Farm, the Jackalopes' yard. You carry the Leygate engineer's spanner to prove it fits.
fixit_farm.descriptionNote: lint fix: no names inside the description (Mara is met at the Counter; Garren left unnamed so the checker passes even though players met him in Allesh-Gilliam)

browsing.line: Walk into the yard and let the Jackalope kid give you the tour.
browsing.logged: A Jackalope kid walked you one fast lap of the yard: the Gullywasher, the Counter, the Arc Bay and the Generator hall.
browsing.note: old line mentioned the MYSTERY bin (a later step) and had no clear verb

gully.line: Go into the Gullywasher and order a drink.
gully.logged: You had a drink at the Gullywasher, served by a Chupacabra bartender.
gully.note: old line gave away the bartender and the house rule

counter.line: Go to the Counter and talk to Mara Quickhands.
counter.logged: At the Counter you met Mara Quickhands, who quotes weight instead of price.
counter.note: old line gave away her answer

arcbay.line: Go to the Arc Bay and talk to Young Gearbox.
arcbay.logged: Young Gearbox poured you a coffee in the Arc Bay, among the rigs.

stabilizer.line: Bring the spanner to Young Gearbox in the Arc Bay, then hear Mara's price for the stabilizer.
stabilizer.logged: You and Mara bargained over the Leyline Stabilizer.
stabilizer.note: plainer; logged neutral across Trade, Shared Oversight, Hard Ask and Delay

bin.line: Reach into the MYSTERY bin by the Counter.
bin.logged: You found the MYSTERY bin by the Counter and decided what to do with it.

laterun.line: Go to the Counter. Mara has a job for you.
laterun.logged: Mara asked you to carry Uncle Thistle to his own wake, and you gave her your answer.
laterun.note: old line gave away the job; logged neutral across take, decline, late and on time

prisoner.line: Ask Young Gearbox about the crying in the back room.
prisoner.logged: In the back room, Mara showed you a bound thief on your territory and asked what justice looks like. You answered.
prisoner.note: old line was long and editorial

load.line: Go to the Arc Bay and load the stabilizer crate.
load.logged: Young Gearbox gave you the stabilizer's certification card, marked TETRARCH, with a message for Garren: sign slow.
load.note: old line gave away the card and the message

settles.line: Take one last look around the Farm before you ride home.
settles.logged: The Farm stopped auditioning you. Mara's ledger has your names in the column that buys drinks.
settles.note: QUESTION for the writer: this beat plays at the Farm with no choices; the old line said ride home, which would send players away before it plays

the_leyline_stabilizer.line: Bargain with Mara for the Leyline Stabilizer.

the_weeping_prisoner.line: Go to the back room with Mara and decide what happens to the person there.

openQuestions: Description: Garren is known from the Allesh-Gilliam quest, so the lint flag was a false positive. I left him unnamed to pass the checker. Say if you would rather write "Garren's spanner" and whitelist it.
load: if the party chose Delay (or never bought the stabilizer) the load step should not be offered. Confirm it is gated on a deal.
Door lines (gullywasher, counter, pip, backstairs, generator, bin) untouched; 'gullywasher' still says 'Oh shit'.

flooded_towns.description: The Water Choir's lean and Sable Nine's chart point the same way, to three towns on the coast road that are under water but not drowned. In the first, Probably Beaumont, one office is still open.
flooded_towns.descriptionNote: old text gave away the final reveal (the mountain's blast cut something in half) and details from later towns

arrive.line: Ride to Probably Beaumont, the first of the three flooded towns, and look around.
arrive.logged: You reached Probably Beaumont. Its streets are under water, but light pulses under the flood in hard shapes along the old civic lines.
arrive.note: old line was a riddle and named the office from the next step

clerk.line: Find the one office still open in Probably Beaumont and talk to Ines Calloway, the Clerk.
clerk.logged: Ines Calloway, the Clerk since the night the sky tore, stamped you a visitor's permit in the only dry room in town.
clerk.note: old line gave away the permits; names Ines because this is her beat

beaumont.line: Decide what to do about the light in Probably Beaumont's streets. Steady the leyflow with care, or ride the surge and harvest what it shows.
beaumont.logged: You dealt with the light in Probably Beaumont's streets, and the town answered.
beaumont.note: old line hinted at the outcome

maybe.line: Go on to the second district, Maybe Beaumont, and decide how to handle what the light is doing to its people.
maybe.logged: In Maybe Beaumont the light was handing people roles, and you decided what to do about it.
maybe.note: old line gave away what the district does before you get there

vote.line: Ask who assigned the roles in Maybe Beaumont.
vote.logged: Ines showed you the minutes. The town voted for the light's plan, forty-one to nine, and she was one of the nine.
vote.note: old line hinted at the answer ('she kept the minutes')

dispatcher.line: Find the booth in Maybe Beaumont where the voice is coming from, and talk to it.
dispatcher.logged: You found the Dispatcher, a voice in the booth and the gutters that keeps rerouting traffic and can't finish its sentence.
dispatcher.note: old line hinted at a hidden option ('if you carry a heading')

barrens.line: Go on to the third town, Bedlam Barrens.
barrens.logged: You reached Bedlam Barrens, where the light runs over dry ground as streets that no map shows.
barrens.note: old line was clever noise and repeated the next step's choice

ground.line: Decide what to do with the pattern in Bedlam Barrens. Ground it and settle it, or break it before it finishes.
ground.logged: You decided what to do with the pattern in Bedlam Barrens.
ground.note: old line named the nine voters as a hint; now neutral

whole.line: Put together what you saw in all three towns.
whole.logged: You put it together. The Khezek Tor seal blast cut through a Spark of Hod, and its pieces have been living in the three towns, trying to become whole again.
whole.note: old line had no real instruction

openQuestions: The quest `hex` is empty, so no `where` is set. If the coast-road ride to Probably Beaumont is played as an anywhere beat, add the exact hex name.

'barrens' and 'ground' both play hod_flooded_bedlam_barrens, and 'arrive' and 'beaumont' both play hod_flooded_probably_beaumont. If the opening beat completes both steps at once, a step could be skipped in 'So far'.
'vote' comes before 'dispatcher', but both are in Maybe Beaumont and the beats don't force that order. Confirm the order.

forgotten_cause.description: The Wendigo on the leyline roads are polite, orderly and helpful, and something about them is off. Every traveler's account of them is missing the same piece.
forgotten_cause.descriptionNote: old text named the long table and your name-card, which players meet later; cut to what is known when the quest opens

off.line: Travel the leyline roads and keep an eye on the Wendigo you meet there.
off.logged: Travelers' accounts of the Wendigo on the leyline roads all miss the same piece. Something about them is off.
off.note: old line asked players to 'say the shape out loud' and described a canteen from the next step; now just a plain instruction

road.line: Meet the Wendigo on the road and talk with them.
road.logged: You met the Wendigo on the road. They were perfectly polite, made no small talk, and walked on down the road in step.
road.note: old line hinted at the outcome (watch what happens to the gift)

dougan.line: Go to the Gullywasher at Furrier's Fixit Farm and tell Dougan about the Wendigo.
dougan.logged: Dougan said someone is doing this region's grieving for it, and doing it badly. He gave you a map to where the leylines knot, where the Wendigo have set a table.
dougan.note: old line asked about 'who kept staging the feud', which isn't in this beat; logged line is true for both the Dougan and Gully versions

table.line: Follow Dougan's map to where the leylines knot and find the Wendigo's table.
table.logged: You found the Wendigo's long table where the leylines knot. Every name-card there is someone this region forgot, and the Wendigo have been holding them.
table.note: old line was a riddle. QUESTION for the writer: fc_bridge_confluence may play anywhere, but the beats don't name the Confluence hex, so `where` is left blank. Add the exact hex name if this is a ride.

seated.line: Let the host seat you, and hear the card at your place read aloud.
seated.logged: The host seated you and read your name-card aloud. Three seats down is a card with a name you buried.
seated.note: small wording change. QUESTION for the writer: this step lists the Restore and Redirect beats as well, so the logged line covers only fc_seated

guests.line: Read the name-cards around the table.
guests.logged: You read the name-cards. The forgotten belong to the towns that refuse to grieve as well as to the region, and you left with three names in your pocket.
guests.note: old line gave away what the cards mean ('an invoice, one client'), which the beat never says

night.line: Ask the Wendigo the name of their night.
night.logged: The Wendigo named their night, Halloween 2077, when the mountain went and the bunker was sealed. The last thing they filed was the reason for an old feud.
night.note: old line told players what the answer would be

decide.line: Decide what happens to everything the Wendigo hold. Restore the node, take it onto yourselves, or break the network.
decide.logged: You decided what happens to everything the Wendigo were holding.
decide.note: old line gave away the Restore outcome (the receipt with a goat)

reason.line: Ride back to the Gullywasher at Furrier's Fixit Farm and see Dougan.
reason.logged: Dougan is setting a room at the Gullywasher, with a Chupacabra at one end, a Jackalope at the other, and the Ledger open between them with its reason column blank.
reason.note: old line had no instruction. The bridge plays anywhere, so `where` is set

ledger.line: Take the room Dougan set at the Gullywasher. Help the Chupacabra and the Jackalope enter the feud's cause in the Ledger.
ledger.logged: You hosted the summit at the Gullywasher, with the Ledger open between the Chupacabra and the Jackalope.
ledger.note: old line hinted at the answer ('read the receipt, by name, no roll')

the_long_table.line: Sit at the Wendigo's table, read the cards, and decide what happens to everything they hold.
the_long_table.note: old line listed outcome names before players had met them; now a plain instruction

close_the_ledger.line: Go to the Gullywasher and help the Chupacabra and the Jackalope enter the feud's cause in the Ledger.
close_the_ledger.note: old line warned about the outcome; now a plain instruction

openQuestions: The GM note in gullywasher_cultural_summit says that after BREAK the quest is already closed and the room never opens. The 'reason' and 'ledger' steps assume the summit happens. Confirm that the Log never shows them after BREAK.

The 'seated' and 'night' steps each list the Restore, Redirect and Break beats, and 'decide' replays the long-table beat. If the decision can land in any of those three steps, the order of 'So far' lines may skip a step. Confirm which beat completes each step.
The quest description calls the giver Dougan, but the first two steps play before you meet him. Confirm when the quest is accepted.

lost_statues.description: The red threads at Lyrenn's low field all lean one way, and they line up with fixed points on Sable Nine's chart. Three of the old stone statues stand that way, and the first is in a plains basin in the Northreach Expanse.
lost_statues.descriptionNote: old text described all three statues, the Spark and the grading before players had met any of them

first.line: Go to the Northreach Expanse and find the first statue in its plains basin.
first.logged: You found the first statue half-sunk in a basin on the Northreach plains, one hand open and one clenched. A Spark of Geburah inside it is awake and waiting.

sexton.line: Follow the broom marks and talk to the old man sweeping the basin.
sexton.logged: An old man called the Sexton sweeps the basin and keeps a thick book. He told you to sign it after, not before.
sexton.note: the beat never names Dunmore Kell, so the line says 'the old man'. The old line hinted at the grading

stand.line: Face the first statue. Stand your ground in silence, or challenge it and take the fragment.
stand.logged: You took the first fragment of Geburah from the statue.
stand.note: old line hinted at the book; now plain

truth.line: Go back to the Sexton and tell him how you got the fragment.

truth.note: old line gave away what he would do

second.line: Climb to the mountain pool above the road in the Inconvenient Mountains and face the second statue.
second.logged: You took the second fragment from the kneeling statue in the mountain pool.
second.note: old line gave away the choices and that the statue had 'already heard'

bleeding.line: Meet Sable Nine on the mountain road. They have come to find you.
bleeding.logged: Sable Nine showed you their chart. Two of their six fixed points are giving off Spark, and they believe the Garden is weakening.

third.line: Go to the third statue, chest-deep in dark mountain water, and decide what you give or take.
third.logged: You took the third fragment from the guardian statue in the dark water.
third.note: the old line told everyone to set down the book, even if they never got it. QUESTION for the writer: the beats don't say which hex this is, so no `where`

whole.line: Bring the three fragments together and make the Spark of Geburah whole.
whole.logged: You made the Spark of Geburah whole. It is watching what you do with it.

terms.note: old line revealed the blank line and hinted at the night's paperwork

gap.line: Stand on the bare plinth at dusk as the sun goes into the sea.
gap.logged: You stood in the gap at dusk, and for one night the count came out right.

age.line: Keep the vigil in the gap until dawn.

age.note: old line revealed the beat and the later rite

tifaret.description: On the road to Furrier's Fixit Farm, a forest opened for you as if it expected you. It is perfectly ordered and calm, and it wants to make you better, which is not the same as wanting you safe.

leave.line: Find your way out of the forest. Talk your way out, or back out the way you came and lose the day.
